purpose: Benchmark tooling ONLY for Miller semantic integration P0 (design §2.4, §4.1). These pins do NOT define the future julie-semantic-sidecar runtime; the sidecar vendors llama.cpp itself and owns its own pin file (scripts/semantic-pins.json, P1).

runtime.name: llama.cpp
runtime.note: llama.cpp publishes no semver 'stable' releases; every master push produces a build-numbered release. The prebuilt archive does NOT contain llama-embedding: that target lives under examples/ and upstream release.yml builds with -DLLAMA_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF. The harness therefore drives the llama-server HTTP embedding endpoint rather than a CLI batch tool. Verified by listing the extracted archive.
runtime.endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings (OpenAI-compatible; requires pooling != none; server L2-normalizes with --embd-normalize 2)

candidates.weight_quant_note: The official Qwen GGUF repo publishes only f16 and Q8_0 — there is NO f32 GGUF. f16 is therefore the highest-precision weight lane available and is what this benchmark runs. Vector-storage precision (f32 vs int8) is varied independently in the lanes, which is what design §2.4 means by 'quantization'.
